title.zh: 一句话如何偷偷加入要求
title.en: How a sentence can smuggle in a demand

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构成年人都愿意在手工活动后继续聊天，一人说：“你刚才解释那种折法很清楚，我想以后有机会再聊。”对方可以愿意聊折纸，却不想约会；也可以欣赏这句话，但没有继续联系的意愿。具体欣赏说的是你注意到了什么，“想再聊”说的是自己的希望；两句都不替对方宣布感受。此处没有确定下一次活动，邀约需要另问。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional adults welcome conversation after a craft activity. One says, “Your explanation of that fold was clear; I would enjoy another conversation sometime.” The other may welcome talking about paper folding without wanting a date, or appreciate the words without wanting further contact. Specific appreciation describes what you noticed; wanting to talk states your own wish. Neither assigns their feelings, and neither settles a future invitation.

title.zh: 在纸上检查一句话就够了
title.en: Checking one sentence on paper is enough

paragraphs.zh: 可以在私人草稿上比较“你肯定也觉得我们很合拍”和“我喜欢刚才那段交流”。前一句替别人作结论，后一句只表达自己的体验。再写一个不需对方回应也成立的结束句，例如“谢谢你分享这个方法”。不必真的发出，也不以收到什么答复检验个人价值。
paragraphs.en: Compare “You must also think we connect well” with “I enjoyed that conversation” on a private draft. The first assigns a conclusion to someone else; the second states your experience. Add an ending that needs no reply, such as “Thank you for sharing that method.” Nothing needs sending, and a response does not test your worth.

title.zh: 连环提问不等于更会聊
title.en: A string of questions is no better conversation

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：虚构的成年人交流中，对方提到在阳台种香草。你可以接“你刚才说那盆换了位置，后来有变化吗？”而不是立刻问住址、能否去家里或为什么没有照片。若对方说只想聊做饭，就顺着新的普通话题，或让对话结束。跟进一个已分享的细节，不等于获得更多私人内容，也不意味着必须连续提出问题才算接住。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene between fictional adults, someone mentions growing herbs on a balcony. “You said you moved that pot; did anything change?” follows a shared detail without asking for an address, a home visit or photographs. If they prefer talking about cooking, follow that ordinary topic or let the exchange end. Following one detail grants no further personal information and requires no continuous questioning.

title.zh: 写一个回应，再写停止的位置
title.en: Draft a reply and a place to stop

paragraphs.zh: 可写两版回应：一版先回答对方已问的普通问题，再接一个相关细节；另一版只回应、不追问。比较两版分别贡献了什么，而不是哪版更能留住对方。对话已经结束时，练习留在纸上，不把新想到的问题当作重新联系的理由。
paragraphs.en: Draft two replies: one answers an ordinary question already asked and follows a relevant detail; the other responds without another question. Compare what each contributes rather than which would keep someone engaged. If the conversation has ended, keep the exercise on paper instead of treating a new question as a reason to reopen contact.

title.zh: 把玩笑变成考试的反例
title.en: When a joke becomes an examination

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：虚构的两位成年人都愿意聊一个夸张的植物标签，你提议给那盆薄荷想一个“小说主角名”。对方说更想知道怎样照顾它，便可以转为普通话题。没有接这个想象，不证明对方无趣、冷淡或与你不合；接了也不说明愿意见面。此处是可不参加的轻松提议，与直接表达好感、跟进内容或安排下一次见面分别理解。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, two fictional adults welcome discussing an elaborate plant label. You offer to invent a novel-character name for the mint. They would rather discuss caring for it, so the conversation can become ordinary. Declining the idea establishes neither dullness, coldness nor incompatibility; joining does not agree to a meeting. This optional playful offer differs from expressing interest, following content or arranging another meeting.

title.zh: 只在纸上写一个轻松版本

paragraphs.zh: 在私人草稿上给同一话题写“玩一下”和“不玩也能继续”的两个版本。例如：“要不要给它起个故事名？”与“这盆植物需要什么光照？”都可不采用。检查笑点是否依赖贬低别人或要求配合；不必为了让聊天活泼而继续制造笑话。
paragraphs.en: Draft a playful and an ordinary version of the same topic, such as “Want to invent a story name for it?” and “What light does this plant need?” Either can be left unused. Check for a joke depending on putting someone down or requiring participation, without making more jokes to maintain a lively exchange.

title.zh: 投入不是对方欠你的答复

paragraphs.zh: 补充原创场景：两位虚构成年人之前都愿意继续认识，一人问是否愿意周末去公开的园艺展。对方回答“也许有空”，这保留未知，不是已经约好；提出别的时间，也不自动意味着接受了活动内容。可以只在明确愿意后再核对具体安排。即使已经买票，投入仍不产生对方必须参加或补偿失望的义务；同意这次活动也不延伸为其他亲密或后续联系。
paragraphs.en: In an additional original scene, fictional adults have welcomed getting acquainted. One asks about a public gardening exhibition at the weekend. “I may be free” leaves the answer open rather than confirming a plan; suggesting another time does not automatically accept the activity. Check arrangements after willingness is clear. Buying a ticket creates no duty to attend or compensate disappointment, and agreement to this activity extends to neither intimacy nor later contact.

title.zh: 用三个虚构回答检查同一句邀请
title.en: Check an invitation against three fictional answers

paragraphs.zh: 给一项虚构邀请写三个清楚状态：“愿意，安排待核对”“不愿意，到此结束”“尚未确定，不算已约好”。这些是练习分类，不要求向真人索取即时答案。若原来已经被拒绝，保留结束状态，不发送修订后的邀请来测试是否改变主意。
paragraphs.en: For a fictional invitation, write three states: “Willing, arrangements still to check”; “Declined, finished”; and “Undecided, not an agreed plan.” These are drafting categories, not a demand for an immediate real response. Keep an existing refusal finished instead of sending a revised invitation to test for a changed mind.
